history: Found as a three-way split at the file-reading seam, one level ABOVE every limit any parser checks. Python and Rust refused at the decoder; the npm CLI and the verify page both substituted U+FFFD and went on to verify the result, so three distinct files shared one claim hash (c856f23670aa3692..) in the two implementations a stranger is most likely to reach. Both JavaScript sides now decode strictly.
note: A single 0xFF inside a string value. Every implementation refuses it, and each refuses at the DECODER rather than at any wire-format limit: Python's CLI raises UnicodeDecodeError out of path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') before load_receipt is called, the Rust CLI reports 'cannot read: stream did not contain valid UTF-8' and exits non-zero, and both JavaScript parsers now say 'receipt is not valid UTF-8'. A receipt is a UTF-8 document; these bytes are not one.
